source.title: On the Impact of the Activation Function on Deep Neural Networks Training
source.authors: Soufiane Hayou; A. Doucet; J. Rousseau

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including supplementary material, is present. No apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents extracting the reported experiments.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how initialization, activation, and adding batch normalization affect deep-network training, using test accuracy and training curves rather than training classification error.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test accuracy, not training classification error. It tests MNIST and CIFAR-10 only, with width 300 and depths up to 200; CIFAR-100 and corrupted or random labels are not tested. The numerical table values are test accuracies.
record.test_reason: The study compares activation-specific Gaussian initializations on the Edge of Chaos (EOC) with ordered-phase initialization, and compares EOC networks with and without batch normalization. Its accuracy-versus-epoch and accuracy-versus-time results bear on V4 and V6. It is not an original source for either version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that EOC initialization accelerates learning, smooth activations improve deep information propagation and empirical performance, and selecting an EOC point according to depth can further help. They report that adding BN worsens learning and increases training time in their experiments. These empirical conclusions use test-accuracy curves, not training classification error.
record.recipe_differences: Studies Gaussian-process signal propagation and EOC initialization, then trains fully connected networks with SGD or RMSProp; reports test accuracy rather than training classification error.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization phase (EOC versus ordered); activation function; adding batch normalization; depth-dependent EOC choice; optimizer and learning rate.

fits_no_version.finding: Under EOC initialization, smooth activations outperform ReLU; supplementary experiments compare RMSProp, x+0.5tanh(x), and modified SiLU.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation choice affects learning speed and test accuracy even among networks using signal-preserving initialization.

record.problems: The reported tables measure test accuracy rather than training error. Experiments cover only MNIST and CIFAR10, with width 300 and depths up to 200. Table 1 and Table 2 report inconsistent CIFAR10 ELU test accuracy at 100 epochs (45.76± 0.91 versus 47.76± 0.91).
record.rows_left_out: None. Extracted 36 rows, below the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error in large convolutional networks, CIFAR-100, label corruption, and the specified size and training-recipe qualifications.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious local minima, and the effect of extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks versus identity-shortcut networks, special deep tanh convolutional initialization, and Fixup.

Orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization at matched variance and training 10,000-layer convolutional networks. Experiments use fully connected networks of width 300 and depth up to 200; they do not measure training classification error.
Stability thresholds, loss catapults, curvature adaptation, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence.
Tolerance of higher learning rates, the named sigmoid/VGG/Inception settings, and normalization-free residual training with Fixup.

missing.what: Matched EOC-versus-ordered-phase accuracy trajectories showing the initialization speed advantage; endpoint tables alone omit this direct comparison.
missing.locator: Figure 5 and Section 4, Initialization on the Edge of Chaos

missing.what: BN-versus-no-BN accuracy trajectories against both epochs and elapsed time, including the explicit finding of longer training time. Current rows record only endpoint test accuracy.
missing.locator: Figure 5, upper and lower panels, and accompanying Section 4 text

missing.what: Tanh accuracy comparisons across EOC bias scales 0.05, 0.2 and 0.5 and depths 30–90 at epochs 10, 50 and 100; the text reports the advantage of choosing initialization according to depth.
missing.locator: Figure 6 and Section 4, Selection of a point on the EOC

record.verdict_notes: ReLU EOC initialization coincides with the He variance prescription, contrary to the record's suggestion that activation-matched initialization is untested. BN comparisons do not establish a limitation of V4 because they change normalization rather than compare initializations. Table 3 contains selected initialization parameters, not accuracy values, and its depth labels conflict with the surrounding prose; those selections should not become performance rows. The source also misnumbers several table references.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error; CIFAR-100; corrupted or random labels; model size, early stopping and regularized recipes.
Two-layer teacher-student problems, spurious minima and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain batch-normalized convolutional networks versus residual shortcuts; ImageNet; the cited special initializations and Fixup recipe.

The study tests Gaussian initialization on or off the Edge of Chaos, but not activation-matched initializations such as He or Glorot, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, or 10,000-layer convolutional networks.
Learning rates above a stability limit, curvature or sharpness dynamics, and the catapult mechanism.
The study compares EOC initialization with EOC plus batch normalization; it does not test the cited sigmoid MNIST, VGG CIFAR-10 or Inception ImageNet settings, nor Fixup.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: EOC initialization, tested MNIST and CIFAR10 settings
reader_labels.reason: The authors state EOC initialization dramatically accelerates training; test accuracy rises across epochs and ordered-phase controls remain near 0.1 (R1, R4, R7, R10, R13, R16, R19-R36). This is indirect evidence for trainability, not a measurement of training error.

reader_labels.reason: Adding BN to the EOC setup gives lower test accuracy for every listed activation and dataset, with a large drop for Tanh (R2, R5, R8, R11, R14, R17).
